Pattern: cherish + N; thường bị động
Examples: The photographs are cherished more than the furniture. | They cherished a routine other people found dull.

Pattern: neglect + N; thường bị động
Examples: The garden was neglected and the children were not. | He neglected his own health while caring for hers.

Pattern: babysit; babysit + sb
Examples: Her father babysits every Thursday. | They babysat the grandchildren for a whole fortnight.

Pattern: mourn + sb; mourn for + sb
Examples: The street mourned him for a month. | She mourned privately and worked as usual.

Pattern: support + sb; thường bị động
Examples: He supported two households on one wage. | She was supported by her sister through the illness.

Pattern: an affectionate + N (family, letter)
Examples: The letters are affectionate and very formal. | He was affectionate in a way his own father had not been.

Pattern: a caring + N (parent, household)
Examples: A caring household is not always a calm one. | She is caring with strangers and brisk with her sons.

Pattern: be protective + of/towards + sb
Examples: He is protective of his younger brother still. | They were protective towards the new arrival.

Pattern: be jealous + of + sb
Examples: She was jealous of the attention and said nothing. | He was never jealous of his brother's success.

Pattern: a distant + N (father, relative)
Examples: Her father was distant and completely reliable. | A distant cousin turned out to be the only witness.

Pattern: a forgiving + N (nature, family)
Examples: She has a forgiving nature and a long memory. | The family is forgiving about everything but money.

Pattern: a dependable + N (brother, neighbour)
Examples: A dependable neighbour is worth nine relatives abroad. | He was dependable in the dull, decisive way.

Pattern: a hospitable + N (family, household)
Examples: The household is hospitable to the point of exhaustion. | They were hospitable to everyone who came off the boat.

Pattern: a reserved + N (manner, family)
Examples: His manner is reserved rather than cold. | A reserved family shows affection by turning up.

Pattern: be inseparable; inseparable + N
Examples: The twins were inseparable until university. | They were inseparable for nine years and then nothing.

Pattern: a well-behaved + N (child, class)
Examples: The children were well-behaved and plainly bored. | A well-behaved child is not always a happy one.

Pattern: a mischievous + N (child, grin)
Examples: He was mischievous rather than disobedient. | A mischievous grandchild livens up the whole visit.

Pattern: grow up; grow up in + N
Examples: She grew up in two rooms above a shop. | They grew up speaking the dialect at home.

Pattern: bring together + N hoặc bring + N + together; tách được
Examples: The illness brought the family together. | One funeral brought nine cousins together.

Pattern: make up; make up with + sb
Examples: They made up at the christening. | He made up with his brother after nine years.

Pattern: put up with + N; không tách được
Examples: She put up with the arrangement for a decade. | They put up with the noise because of the children.

Pattern: watch over + sb; không tách được
Examples: She watched over both parents at once. | Neighbours watched over the children all summer.

Pattern: drop in on + sb; không tách được
Examples: Her aunt drops in on them most Sundays. | They dropped in on the old neighbour every winter.

Pattern: fall for + sb; không tách được
Examples: She fell for him at a wedding. | He fell for her over nine months of letters.

Pattern: split up; split up with + sb
Examples: They split up after eleven years. | She split up with him and kept the flat.

Pattern: move in with + sb; không tách được
Examples: He moved in with his daughter after the fall. | They moved in with her parents to save for a deposit.

Pattern: name + sb + after + sb; tách được
Examples: The boy was named after his grandfather. | They named her after a street in the old town.

Pattern: be/need + a shoulder to cry on
Examples: Her sister was a shoulder to cry on for thirty years. | Everybody needs a shoulder to cry on at some point.

Pattern: stand by sb + through thick and thin
Examples: They stood by each other through thick and thin. | She supported the family through thick and thin.

Pattern: have + a soft spot for + sb
Examples: He has a soft spot for his youngest niece. | She had a soft spot for the difficult one.

Pattern: bury the hatchet
Examples: They buried the hatchet at their mother's funeral. | Nobody suggested burying the hatchet for nine years.

Pattern: keep in touch + with + sb
Examples: They kept in touch by letter for forty years. | She keeps in touch with every cousin abroad.

Term: like two peas in a pod
Definition: giống nhau như hai giọt nước
Pattern: be + like two peas in a pod
Examples: The brothers are like two peas in a pod. | Grandmother and granddaughter were like two peas in a pod.

Definition: chốn thân thuộc như nhà mình
Pattern: be + a home from home
Examples: Her aunt's kitchen was a home from home. | The club became a home from home for the new arrivals.

Pattern: take sides + in + N
Examples: The cousins refused to take sides in the dispute. | Taking sides in a family quarrel costs you both.
